Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Simple epithelium is composed of a single layer of cells and functions as a lining for body cavities, ducts, and tubes.

Statement II: Compound epithelium consists of two or more cell layers and has a protective function as in the dry surface of the skin.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Epithelial tissues provide a covering or lining for body parts and are divided into simple and compound epithelia based on the number of cell layers.

Step 2: Evaluation of Epithelial Layers
Simple epithelium is indeed made of a single layer of cells lining body cavities, ducts, and tubes. Compound epithelium consists of two or more layers of cells (multi-layered) and primarily provides protection against chemical and mechanical stresses, such as on the dry surface of the skin.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both biological assertions are accurate.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Exocrine glands lack ducts and secrete hormones directly into the fluid bathing the gland.

Statement II: Endocrine glands release mucus, saliva, earwax, oil, milk, and digestive enzymes through ducts or tubes.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Glands are classified into exocrine and endocrine categories based on whether their secretions are poured through ducts or directly into surrounding fluid.

Step 2: Evaluation of Glandular Modes
Exocrine glands possess ducts or tubes through which they release products such as mucus, saliva, earwax, oil, milk, and digestive enzymes. Conversely, endocrine glands do not have ducts and secrete hormones directly into the fluid bathing the gland. Both claims reverse these definitions.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both biological assertions are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Connective tissues are the most abundant and widely distributed tissues in the body of complex animals.

Statement II: In all connective tissues including blood, the cells secrete fibres of structural proteins called collagen or elastin.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Connective tissues link and support other tissues or organs, and most types contain structural protein fibres that provide strength, elasticity, and flexibility.

Step 2: Evaluation of Fibre Secretion
Connective tissues are indeed the most abundant and widely distributed tissues in complex animals. However, cells secrete collagen or elastin fibres in all connective tissues EXCEPT blood; blood is a fluid connective tissue whose cells do not secrete structural protein fibres.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The assertion about abundance and distribution is correct, whereas the assertion claiming blood cells secrete collagen or elastin fibres is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Adhering junctions facilitate cells to communicate with each other by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells for rapid ion transfer.

Statement II: Tight junctions help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Specialised junctions (tight, adhering, and gap) provide structural and functional links between individual epithelial cells.

Step 2: Evaluation of Junction Roles
Connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells for rapid transfer of ions and small molecules is the function of gap junctions, not adhering junctions (which perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells together). Tight junctions do indeed stop substances from leaking across a tissue.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The assertion regarding adhering junctions is incorrect, whereas the assertion regarding tight junctions is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURALORGANISATIONINANIMALS_MCQ_Q05 - Embryonic cartilage replacement and bone marrow

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Most of the cartilages in vertebrate embryos are replaced by bones in adults.

Statement II: The bone marrow in some bones is the site of production of blood cells.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cartilage and bone are specialised structural connective tissues with distinct developmental and physiological roles.

Step 2: Evaluation of Cartilage and Bone
In vertebrate embryos, most of the cartilaginous skeleton is replaced by bone in adults, leaving cartilage only at specific sites such as the nose tip, outer ear joints, and intervertebral joints. Additionally, bone marrow in certain bones serves as the site of blood cell production.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both biological assertions are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURALORGANISATIONINANIMALS_MCQ_Q06 - Smooth and cardiac muscle striations and control

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Smooth muscle fibres show prominent striations and are under direct voluntary control.

Statement II: Cardiac muscle tissue is found in both the walls of internal organs like the stomach and in the heart.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Muscle tissues are distinguished by the presence or absence of striations, voluntary or involuntary control, and anatomical location.

Step 2: Evaluation of Muscle Properties
Smooth muscle fibres are non-striated and involuntary, meaning their contraction cannot be directly controlled by conscious thought. Cardiac muscle tissue is a contractile tissue present ONLY in the heart, whereas the stomach wall contains smooth muscle tissue.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both biological assertions are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Neurons are the unit of the neural system and are excitable cells that exert the greatest control over the body's responsiveness.

Statement II: Neuroglial cells generate electrical disturbances along their plasma membranes faster than neurons.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Neural tissue consists of excitable neurons and supporting neuroglial cells.

Step 2: Evaluation of Excitability
Neurons are indeed the functional units of the neural system and are excitable cells that control the body's responsiveness to changing conditions. In contrast, neuroglial cells do not generate electrical disturbances; they protect and support neurons.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The assertion about neurons is correct, whereas the assertion about neuroglial cells generating electrical disturbances is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURALORGANISATIONINANIMALS_MCQ_Q08 - Skeletal and cardiac muscle junctional features

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Skeletal muscle fibres taper at both ends and lack striations.

Statement II: In cardiac muscle, cell junctions fuse the plasma membranes of adjacent cells and communication junctions allow them to contract as a unit.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Skeletal, smooth, and cardiac muscles differ in cell shape, striations, and intercellular junctions.

Step 2: Evaluation of Cell Shapes and Junctions
Skeletal muscle fibres are long, cylindrical, and striated (striped), whereas tapering fusiform non-striated fibres belong to smooth muscle. In cardiac muscle, cell junctions fuse plasma membranes and intercalated discs act as communication junctions enabling contraction as a single unit.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The assertion regarding skeletal muscle shape and striations is incorrect, whereas the assertion regarding cardiac muscle junctions is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURALORGANISATIONINANIMALS_MCQ_Q09 - Typhlosole and respiratory surface in earthworm

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: In earthworms, the typhlosole is an internal median fold of the dorsal intestinal wall that increases the effective area of absorption.

Statement II: Earthworms lack specialised breathing devices, so respiratory exchange occurs through their moist body surface into the bloodstream.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Earthworms possess specialised anatomical adaptations for both nutrient absorption in the intestine and cutaneous gas exchange.

Step 2: Evaluation of Digestive and Respiratory Adaptations
After the 26th segment (except the last 23rd–25th segments), the dorsal wall of the intestine forms an internal median fold called the typhlosole, increasing the effective absorptive area. Because earthworms lack specialised breathing organs, respiratory gas exchange occurs across their moist body surface directly into their closed bloodstream.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both biological assertions are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Pheretima exhibits an open blood vascular system in which visceral organs are bathed in haemolymph.

Statement II: Development of earthworms is indirect, involving a free-swimming larval stage before forming the adult.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Earthworms have a closed circulatory system and undergo direct embryonic development inside cocoons.

Step 2: Evaluation of Circulatory and Developmental Traits
Pheretima exhibits a closed blood vascular system where blood is confined to the heart and blood vessels (open circulation with haemolymph occurs in arthropods such as cockroaches). Furthermore, development in earthworms is direct, meaning no larva is formed.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both biological assertions are incorrect.

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: In Periplaneta americana, the first pair of wings arises from the mesothorax and is opaque, dark, and leathery, covering the hind wings at rest.

Statement II: The hind wings arise from the prothorax and are thick and opaque to protect the abdomen during flight.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The thorax of a cockroach consists of prothorax, mesothorax, and metathorax, with wings borne on the mesothorax and metathorax.

Step 2: Evaluation of Wing Origins and Structure
The forewings (tegmina) arise from the mesothorax and are opaque, dark, and leathery, covering the hind wings at rest. However, the hind wings arise from the metathorax (not the prothorax) and are transparent and membranous for flight.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The assertion about mesothoracic forewings (tegmina) is correct, whereas the assertion about hind wings arising from the prothorax and being thick and opaque is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: In earthworms, septal nephridia are attached to the lining of the body wall from segment 3 to the last and open on the body surface.

Statement II: Four pairs of spermathecae are located in the 6th–9th segments to receive and store spermatozoa during copulation.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Earthworms possess three types of nephridia based on segmental location and opening, as well as paired spermathecae for sperm storage.

Step 2: Evaluation of Nephridia and Spermathecae
Nephridia attached to the body wall lining from segment 3 to the last that open on the body surface are integumentary nephridia, not septal nephridia (septal nephridia occur on intersegmental septa from segment 15 onwards and open into the intestine). Conversely, four pairs of spermathecae are indeed located in segments 6–9 to receive and store spermatozoa during copulation.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The assertion about septal nephridia is incorrect, whereas the assertion about spermathecae is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURALORGANISATIONINANIMALS_MCQ_Q13 - Open circulation and uricotelic excretion in cockroach

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: In cockroaches, blood from sinuses enters the funnel-shaped heart chambers through ostia and is pumped anteriorly to the sinuses again.

Statement II: Malpighian tubules are lined by glandular and ciliated cells that absorb nitrogenous wastes and convert them into uric acid, making the cockroach uricotelic.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cockroaches have an open circulatory system with haemocoel and perform excretion primarily through Malpighian tubules.

Step 2: Evaluation of Circulation and Excretion
The elongated muscular heart of cockroach consists of funnel-shaped chambers with ostia on either side; haemolymph from sinuses enters through ostia and is pumped anteriorly back to sinuses. Malpighian tubules are lined by glandular and ciliated cells that absorb nitrogenous wastes and convert them into uric acid excreted via the hindgut, making the insect uricotelic.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both biological assertions are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURALORGANISATIONINANIMALS_MCQ_Q14 - Frog intestine length and aestivation respiration

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: The alimentary canal of a frog is very long because frogs are strictly herbivorous animals.

Statement II: During aestivation and hibernation, gaseous exchange in frogs takes place primarily through pulmonary respiration using the lungs.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The anatomy and respiratory modes of frogs reflect their carnivorous diet and amphibious seasonal adaptations.

Step 2: Evaluation of Diet and Dormancy Respiration
The alimentary canal of a frog is short (not long) because frogs are carnivores, reducing the length of the intestine. Furthermore, during aestivation (summer sleep) and hibernation (winter sleep) in deep burrows, gaseous exchange takes place through the skin (cutaneous respiration), not through the lungs.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both biological assertions are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURALORGANISATIONINANIMALS_MCQ_Q15 - Female frog reproductive and urinary ducts

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: In female frogs, the ovaries are situated near the kidneys and have no functional connection with them.

Statement II: In female frogs, the ureters act as urinogenital ducts that carry both urine and ova together into the cloaca.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Unlike male frogs, where testes connect to kidneys via vasa efferentia, female frogs maintain completely separate urinary and reproductive tracts.

Step 2: Evaluation of Female Ducts
In female frogs, the ovaries lie near the kidneys with no functional connection to them. A pair of oviducts arising from the ovaries opens into the cloaca separately from the ureters; thus, the ureters do not act as urinogenital ducts in females.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The assertion that female ovaries have no functional connection with kidneys is correct, whereas the assertion that female ureters act as urinogenital ducts is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURALORGANISATIONINANIMALS_MCQ_Q16 - Frog heart chambers and limb digits

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: The hind limbs of a frog end in four digits, whereas the larger and more muscular forelimbs end in five digits.

Statement II: The heart of a frog has three chambers—two atria and one ventricle—and is covered by a membrane called pericardium.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Frogs have pentadactyl/tetradactyl limb adaptations for swimming and leaping, and a three-chambered heart enclosed in pericardium.

Step 2: Evaluation of Limbs and Heart
In frogs, the hind limbs are larger and muscular and end in FIVE digits (with webbed feet for swimming), whereas the forelimbs end in FOUR digits. Meanwhile, the heart is indeed three-chambered (two atria and one ventricle) and covered by pericardium.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The assertion regarding limb digit counts is incorrect, whereas the assertion regarding heart chambers and pericardium is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
